answer: Sybil resistance via a bonded identity with a cryptographic 'cipher' of verifiable commitments. Each identity posts a secret-hash commitment, so a farm can't quietly spawn many without revealing a linkable structure. Weight scales with time-bonded stake, not raw count, and each epoch identities are sharded across a 'canyon' of random validator groups so a cluster can't corner consensus. A newcomer must prove a 'haven' of clean history — no prior slashes, no shared commitment roots — before earning weight. Attacker cost: locked stake plus a commitment graph that links its own fakes.
